Build only this feature on this page. Get it working, test it, and then move on.

What you are building

Use the existing modal and browser flow to create a new task in JSON storage and then prove the new record appears back in the list. You are rebuilding the same feature with JSON storage, so keep the user experience aligned while the persistence model changes.

The key idea for this feature is POST requests, id management, and safe JSON append logic.. Before you write anything, make sure you can describe what the user should see or what the request should do when this feature is finished.

Key words and definitions

TermMeaning
POST requestA request used to create a new record.
PayloadThe data sent with the request.
InsertAdding a new record to storage.
RefreshUpdating the interface so the new record is visible.

Why this still matters to the client

  • Staff still need to create tasks quickly and trust that the record was saved.
  • This feature is where JSON identifier management becomes a real design decision rather than a theory note.

What to carry in from earlier pages

  • Reuse the same modal and field mapping from the SQL track.
  • Bring forward the Python JSON practice page so the read-edit-write cycle feels familiar.

POST request terms

  • request.get_json() reads the JSON body Flask received.
  • Content-Type: application/json tells the server how to interpret the body.
  • After a create action, the UI should prove success by reloading the list.

Create flow outcome

The important moment is not the click. It is the new record appearing back in the list after storage succeeds.

Save task Writes to JSON
New task now visible in the list

How this feature moves through the stack

HTMLJavaScriptFlaskStorageResponse

Useful reference before you code

  • A create flow starts in the form, passes through the backend, and ends with refreshed evidence on screen.
  • Front-end validation improves usability, but back-end validation still matters.
  • The class should be able to trace where every submitted value goes.
  • When creating a record in JSON storage, identifier management and file integrity need explicit care.

Generic create-request pattern

const payload = { title, priority };

fetch("/api/items", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
  },
  body: JSON.stringify(payload)
}).then(() => loadItems());
payload

This is the JavaScript object you want to send to the backend.

method: "POST"

POST is the HTTP method commonly used when creating a new record.

Content-Type

This header tells the server the request body contains JSON.

JSON.stringify

Turns the JavaScript object into JSON text for the request body.

Build it in this order

Creating in JSON is still a chain: read values, build payload, append carefully, save, then redraw.

Step 1 static/js/app.js

Read the modal values and send the POST request

  • Reuse the same control ids and payload-building habit from the SQL track.
  • Keep the request body focused on the values the backend genuinely needs.
Step 2 app.py

Load the existing records and choose the next id

  • Read the existing task list before creating the new object.
  • Decide how the next identifier will be produced safely and consistently.
  • Convert values into the types the JSON structure should store.

Ask yourself

  • What goes wrong if every new task always uses the same id?
  • Why might a select value need type conversion before storage?
Step 3 app.py

Append, save, and return success

  • Add the new object to the Python list, then write the whole structure back to disk.
  • Return a success response the browser can use to reload evidence on screen.

Where the checks happen

HTML

The interface can require fields, constrain control types, and guide the user before submit.

JavaScript

The browser can check presence, shape, and request timing before sending data.

Flask

The backend must re-check the request because outside tools can bypass the browser entirely.

JSON write step

The document write logic must reject or repair bad structures before saving.

Where your work goes

File or areaWhy this file mattersWhat belongs in this feature
static/js/app.jsReads the modal values and sends the POST requestBuild the payload clearly and refresh the list after success
app.pyCreates the new JSON-backed recordChoose the next id, validate the values, append, and save
data/tasks.jsonStores the updated task listThe new object should appear here after the write

When this feature is ready to sign off

  • A valid modal submission creates one new stored record.
  • The new id is unique and consistent.
  • The list redraw gives visible evidence that creation worked.
